examples.description: 100 / 1,000 / 10,000 instances with no, one, three and noise deformers as presets.
examples.name: Procedural Benchmark

examples.description: Point and box swarms from 1,000 to 1,000,000 instances with GPU culling and LOD, driven by curl noise and vortex fields.
examples.name: Stress Test (1K to 1M)

examples.description: Three copies of one CC0 character, idling, walking and running from the same glTF skin: 49 joints, three clips, GPU skinning through the shared PBR shading. Each node declares its own opening state, and the pose is a pure function of the timeline, so the window and an offline render agree.
examples.name: Alien - Skinned Character

examples.description: Six modular aliens from one 89-joint rig, each playing a different one of its 26 clips: idle, walking, crazy, jet flight, a fight stance and a run. Six independent skeletons in one frame.
examples.name: Alien Squad - Modular Characters

examples.description: The diagnostic environment for character problems: clip playback, root motion made visible (an in-place clip beside Dying_forward and Landing, each on its own origin pip), four yaws, three scales, and the farm pack for telling an asset bug from a systemic one. Neutral ground and studio light on purpose -- the character is the subject. Contracts and regression tests in docs/character-animation-lab.md.
examples.name: Character Animation Lab

examples.description: One instance of every animal in the imported farm pack, in profile and to scale: a 1.77 m bull down to a 0.11 m chick, each playing the one clip its rig carries. The validation scene for the conversion, not a dressed environment.
examples.name: Farm Animals - Imported Pack

examples.description: Prototype: two copies of one rigged low-poly astronaut, one playing a keyboard on an X-stand and one a five-piece drum kit, each driven by a Mixamo clip retargeted onto the astronaut's own skeleton and played through the glTF skin path. The meshes are built outside the repository by tools/make_astronaut_musicians.py; without them the scene shows only its floor.
examples.name: Astronaut Musicians - Prototype

examples.description: Every primitive, distribution, variation control, deformer and stack, with audio routes and a performance readout.
examples.name: Procedural Geometry Lab

examples.description: A deliberately difficult renderer test scene with near/far/behind-camera geometry, a skinned alien, transparency and particles.
examples.name: Renderer QA

examples.description: The entity layer end to end (ADR-088): a character picks navigable destinations from the same WorldMap the terrain mesh was built from, stops to look at a hovering scout, and walks faster as the track opens up -- because a behaviour's speed is an ordinary parameter and the music can reach it. The scout's four materials answer four different bands.
examples.name: Wanderer - Behaviour and Navigation

examples.description: Procedural organism look-dev: the tube primitive and the gill structure, kept as a test rather than a showcase.
examples.name: Bioluminescent World

examples.description: Five glowing fungi: a stem and a domed cap, both the same swept-curve primitive with a radius profile.
examples.name: Fungi

examples.description: The same painterly scene and camera using the PBR surface mode, for controlled style comparisons.
examples.name: Glowmere Valley - Matched PBR

examples.description: A cool alien valley with a warm luminous crown, broad foliage shapes, soft lighting bands and an analytic night sky.
examples.name: Glowmere Valley - Painterly

examples.description: One machined part on a plinth under two softboxes: the benchmark for whether a single object can be made to look photographed rather than generated.
examples.name: Hero Metal

examples.description: Trunk, boughs and tendrils, all one swept-curve primitive: the geometry foundation for the ecosystem work.
examples.name: Organic Curves

examples.description: Three individuals of one species from the same grammar and different seeds -- recursive branching with no bespoke code.
examples.name: Plant Grammar

examples.description: The same valley spread over 840 m: 99,515 placed, 1,352 visible, 27.6 ms. Identical art direction, four times the ground.
examples.name: Glowmere Density - Dense

examples.description: 1,100 m of the same valley: 160,766 placed, 3,111 visible, 33.6 ms -- heavier than the authored showcase scene. The renderer's stress rung.
examples.name: Glowmere Density - Extreme

examples.description: Glowmere thinned to 40% of its density weights over the same 420 m of ground: 1,665 instances placed, 94 visible, 10.7 ms at 1440x900. The lightest rung of the renderer's density ladder.
examples.name: Glowmere Density - Low

examples.description: Glowmere at its shipped density over 420 m: 10,123 placed, 595 visible, 14.1 ms. The reference rung -- every other rung is this one scaled.
examples.name: Glowmere Density - Medium

examples.description: Photogrammetry rocks, roots and vegetation from Poly Haven, placed and varied procedurally under a nocturne rig.
examples.name: Bioluminescent Grove

examples.description: A world built in order: geography, then biomes derived from it, then an ecology that reads the same biome weights the ground is coloured with. 38,000 instances of a CC0 library, lit by a low moon.
examples.name: Glowmere Valley

examples.description: The bioluminescent valley with a finished 2D composition over it: a tracked-out title card, four lyric lines with staggered entrances and exits, and a thin border that fades up over the first two and a half seconds. The beat reaches the type through an ordinary modulation route, the same way it reaches the world.
examples.name: Glowmere Valley - Lyrics

examples.description: The successor valley: a river that enters at one edge of the map, meanders 700 m down a descending course and leaves at the opposite edge, with the terrain shaped against it rather than around it. Same palette, same moon, same emission ladder as the painterly scene; new geography, and the three heroes that were a torus, a tube and nine spheres are gone.
examples.name: Glowmere Valley 2

examples.description: Glowmere Valley 2 directed by three cameras (ADR-245). Hero Free Roam is the Auto-director's camera, unchanged. Valley Wide is an authored establishing shot, keyframed on the ordinary timeline and placed by authored shots. UFO Watch rides the saucer and takes the frame whenever the abduction scenario reaches its beam -- an event claiming the cut, not a special case in the code.
examples.name: Glowmere Valley 2 - Multi-Camera

examples.description: Glowmere Valley 3, a 3:45 music video to "Rebuild": 73 locked shots cut to the song, five UFO set pieces and the hero pulses, generated from the multi-camera valley by tools/make_glowmere_valley_3.py. The song is not in the repository: it plays when Rebuild.mp3 is on the Desktop (docs/glowmere-valley-3/README.md).
examples.name: Glowmere Valley 3

examples.description: Glowmere at night with ADR-230's atmospheric effects: an audio-reactive aurora rising from the horizon, and bioluminescent comets crossing the sky -- one hero, one rainbow, and a three-comet burst, all launched by sequencer events.
examples.name: Glowmere Atmospherics

examples.description: Combined procedural geometry and audio modulation, timeline-driven.
examples.name: Hyperspace

examples.description: Nested procedural geometry at extreme scale differences, camera inside.
examples.name: Impossible Chamber

examples.description: A metallic assembly that separates into thousands of parts, floats, gathers and locks back together, then detonates; disassembly is a field, so assembled is simply zero strength.
examples.name: Metallic Reassembly

examples.description: A sequenced music video (ADR-089): five shots cut to a generated song's own sections, a recurring character who walks a stylised miniature city from dusk to night, a camera that follows and then reveals, sixteen lyric lines, a title, a border, and four small audio-reactive relationships. The whole piece is one seq::Sequence baked onto the ordinary timeline, so the frame at any second is a pure evaluation.
examples.name: Night Shift

examples.description: Large-scale radial architectural composition with arches and a free camera.
examples.name: The Cathedral

examples.description: Spiral instancing and continuous deformation with a travelling camera.
examples.name: The Helix

examples.description: The flagship world: radial colonnades, rings, arches, spiral corridors and recursive chambers driven by fields, with seven world macros, eight states and a four-minute cue arc.
examples.name: The Infinite Temple

examples.description: A particle sculpture that performs its own score. Three logarithmic spiral arms authored as splines, carried by a differentially rotating field around a hot core; an onset launches a radial wave that crosses the sculpture at 19 m/s, so a beat reaches the rim a second and a half after the centre. 190,000 particles, no C++.
examples.name: The Living Constellation

examples.description: A forty-second shot: a cast-iron vessel with a furnace belt, on a deck in a dark hall. Manual exposure, a re-aimed IndustrialCold rig, layered materials and a four-beat cue arc.
examples.name: The Living Machine

examples.description: Audio-reactive procedural architecture: radial colonnade, rings, fog, particles, bloom.
examples.name: The Temple

examples.description: The authored Tree of Life hero export -- 3.16 M triangles, seven meshes -- standing on a floating island in cosmic space, the island turning once every three minutes and breathing on a forty-second swell. The tree is a child of the island's transform and never moves of its own accord. A celestial key falls diagonally across tree and island from a hundred degrees off the camera, throwing the canopy's shadow off the far edge of the plateau; the underside is left to the sky's ground hemisphere. Bare landmass, a shell of 1,700 points for stars; nothing else in frame.
examples.name: Tree of Life - Floating Island

examples.description: The same island, the same three lights, the same parameters at their other values: the celestial key drops to a third of its daylight strength and turns cool blue, the fill follows it, the shadows deepen and the star shells come up. One framework, two states -- not two lighting systems. Also reachable as the 'Celestial Night' preset inside the day project.
examples.name: Tree of Life - Celestial Night

examples.description: The same Tree of Life and island, now suspended above an endless sea under a full day/night cycle. One dayPhase parameter drives sky, sun, moon, stars, atmosphere, water and the tree's bioluminescence together, wrapping seamlessly at midnight; the night sky and its moon are an HDRI the water reflects, and the moonlight is a real shadow-casting key aimed along that moon. Scrub the cycle or let it run.
examples.name: Tree of Life - Ocean World

examples.description: One scene, four presets: Cathedral, Temple, Helix, Hyperspace morph into each other on a timeline.
examples.name: Worlds (preset morph)

examples.description: Quality Lab benchmark 1: thin fence slats, a receding tile grid, shallow diagonal edges and small emissive spheres, all crossing the sampling limit inside one frame. Static free camera.
examples.name: Quality Lab: aliasing

examples.description: Quality Lab benchmark 2: the aliasing subject on a lateral spline dolly, so the velocity AOV, the disocclusion mask and the motion-compensated residual have real motion to measure.
examples.name: Quality Lab: aliasing dolly

examples.description: Four layers of one shower: 34 k wrapping drops in a camera-following volume, an out-of-focus near layer, a ripple for every drop that lands, and the mist it has already wetted. Particle size drives fall speed, so the streaks have a spread of lengths rather than one.
examples.name: Rain

examples.description: A flake is a tumbling card, not a streak; small dense flakes fall fast and large ones hang, so the field reads as falling rather than scrolling. A hundred and fifty huge out-of-focus flakes ride with the lens.
examples.name: Snow

examples.description: Dark ash read as an absence of light against a burning sky, embers on independent flicker phases from two sources at different distances, and the smoke they rise out of. Temperature is the ember colour curve.
examples.name: Ashfall

examples.description: A planar travelling wave field IS the squall line: rain spawns where it is, lifted dust spawns where it is not, and both subscribe to the same field, so the moment the rain arrives is the moment the dust stops.
examples.name: Weather front

examples.description: Motes lit by a Henyey-Greenstein phase against the key light: quiet across the sun and blazing into it, with a colonnade to cut the light into bands. The same population, and only the angle changes.
examples.name: Dust motes

examples.description: Nine and fourteen persistent swarms that dart and hang on their own phases; one chorus flashes almost together and one twinkles at random, and the only difference between them is pulseSync.
examples.name: Fireflies

examples.description: One airborne biological system authored three ways -- buoyancy as a positive gravity against a high drag, so a grain finds a level and hangs there instead of falling.
examples.name: Pollen, spores and seeds

examples.description: One continuous knob from high summer to deep winter: canopy, undergrowth, ground, sky, fog, pollen, leaf fall and snow are all targets of a single world macro. No winter scene exists.
examples.name: Season shift

examples.description: Procedural Space POC (proto/procedural-space): ray-marched impossible architecture whose spatial rules follow the music. One SDF node morphs between a hall, a rotunda, a recursive cathedral and a lattice on sections and drops; bass widens, mids bend and tighten repetition, highs add recursion and edge light.
examples.name: Procedural Space (POC)

examples.description: The Sonic Garden POC (ADR-1020): one MIDI phrase through a pad, an FM bell, a distorted bass and noisy percussion. The Sonic Character, the notes' musical context and the interpret source's visual families drive a hero form, organic and crystalline structures, shards, spores and the camera. Variants per sound are in sonic-garden/variants/; the audio comes from tools/make_sonic_material.py.
examples.name: Sonic Garden

examples.description: Play the Sonic Garden live (ADR-1025): a MIDI keyboard and a synth's audio input drive the same Sonic Character, musical context and worlds as the file version. Opening it turns live input on; pick the devices in the Live panel (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/LIVE-QUICKSTART.md.
examples.name: Sonic Live

examples.description: On an endless salt flat at dusk the sky is the instrument: chords paint it, melodies fall through it as meteors, the bass makes the horizon shimmer, and a black monolith answers the drums. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/SCENE-CATALOG.md.
examples.name: Sonic VFX - Salt Flat Mirage

examples.description: Each note releases a paper lantern from the surface of a still lake at dusk; the melody becomes a drifting constellation, and the bass a slow swell beneath it. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/SCENE-CATALOG.md.
examples.name: Sonic VFX - Lantern Lake

examples.description: Over a frozen lake the aurora is the pad: chords hang curtains of light, the melody ripples them, the hats are diamond dust glittering in the air, and the snare cracks the ice with light. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/SCENE-CATALOG.md.
examples.name: Sonic VFX - Aurora Tundra

examples.description: A colossal fungal organism hangs from the roof of a flooded cavern and breathes with the bass; melodies climb its hanging threads as light. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/SCENE-CATALOG.md.
examples.name: Sonic VFX - The Breathing Deep

examples.description: Two kilometres down, a colony of siphonophores answers the melody in pulses of cold light while marine snow falls through the hats. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/SCENE-CATALOG.md.
examples.name: Sonic VFX - Abyssal Bloom

examples.description: Black sand on a resonating plate: every note sings its own standing-wave figure into the sand, and a chord is two figures at war. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/SCENE-CATALOG.md.
examples.name: Sonic VFX - Cymatic Plate

examples.description: Silk ribbons draw the melody in the air of an empty theatre: pitch is height, legato is one unbroken stroke, and the kick cracks the ribbons like whips. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/SCENE-CATALOG.md.
examples.name: Sonic VFX - Silk Theatre

examples.description: A black magnetic liquid listens: each note pulls a spike from its surface, and harmony shapes the crown. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/SCENE-CATALOG.md.
examples.name: Sonic VFX - Ferrofluid Crown

examples.description: A single glyph of light inside a video feedback loop: the music turns, zooms and recolours the loop, so the world is the instrument's own echo. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/SCENE-CATALOG.md.
examples.name: Sonic VFX - Feedback Mirror

examples.description: Twelve Tesla towers stand in a ring round a humming core, one for each pitch class; every chord is drawn in lightning, so harmony has a shape. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/SCENE-CATALOG.md.
examples.name: Sonic VFX - Tesla Choir

examples.description: A landscape of pure measurement, barcode ridges and numerals to the horizon, written and erased by the music. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/SCENE-CATALOG.md.
examples.name: Sonic VFX - Datascape

examples.description: The morning after the fire: the bass is the wind breathing on the embers, the snare a flare-up in the black trunks, the melody one ember dancing through the smoke. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/SCENE-CATALOG.md.
examples.name: Sonic VFX - Ember Forest

examples.description: A cathedral drawn in lines of light decays into data under the drums and rebuilds itself on held chords. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/SCENE-CATALOG.md.
examples.name: Sonic VFX - The Corrupted Cathedral

examples.description: A supercell walks across the night prairie: the bass winds its funnel, the snare strikes, and the melody crawls as light inside the cloud. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/SCENE-CATALOG.md.
examples.name: Sonic VFX - Storm Cell

examples.description: Inside a pillar of gas, chords ignite newborn stars: their number is the polyphony, their colour the pitch, and the bass is the density of the cloud. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/SCENE-CATALOG.md.
examples.name: Sonic VFX - Stellar Nursery

examples.description: A black hole drinks a disk of light: every note is a star that falls into it, and the bass is the hole's own mass bending the sky. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/SCENE-CATALOG.md.
examples.name: Sonic VFX - Event Horizon

examples.description: The Golden Passage: you fly through an endless luminous sculpture of sacred geometry, rose-window gates strung on twelve helical rails; a chord lights its own polygon of rails down the whole passage, the kick sends a wave of light ahead of you, the bass widens the passage. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/ABSTRACT-PLAN.md.
examples.name: Sonic Abstract - Sacred Geometry Flight

examples.description: Pulsar Plain: a poster you can fly through. Hidden-line ridgelines ripple to the horizon under a colossal outline circle; the drums build flat blocks of one bold colour. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/ABSTRACT-PLAN.md.
examples.name: Sonic Abstract - Neon Vector World

examples.description: Candy Archipelago: a toy island floating in a candy sky, inked and cel-shaded, where three round creatures sing the notes, hop on the kick and the giant flower blooms when the sound is held. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/ABSTRACT-PLAN.md.
examples.name: Sonic Abstract - Cel-Shaded Dream World

examples.description: Chromatic Corridor: monumental portals of pure colour flow toward you forever through coloured haze, each a step further round the colour wheel, toward a blinding light. The music breathes the corridor's spacing, winds its twist and recolours the space itself. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/ABSTRACT-PLAN.md.
examples.name: Sonic Abstract - Infinite Color Geometry

examples.description: Lantern Reef: a macro view into a twilight meadow of translucent organisms that breathe, bloom and sway with the music; the notes open flowers, the kick blooms the lantern, held sound makes it grow. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/ABSTRACT-PLAN.md.
examples.name: Sonic Abstract - Organic Digital Garden

examples.description: Glass Caldera: a digital painting of faceted mountains round a mirror lake, flown through at dusk. The music raises slow waves of topography that roll out from the island through every range; onsets drop rings of light on the water and send light out through the ranges. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/ABSTRACT-PLAN.md.
examples.name: Sonic Abstract - Digital Alpine

examples.description: Contour Valley: a landscape as a sculptural colour field. You skim a glowing river down a winding valley between smooth hills coloured by their height in hard bands, ruled with contour lines that flow up the slopes with the music; the river rises and brightens with the bass. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/ABSTRACT-PLAN.md.
examples.name: Sonic Abstract - Chromatic Topography

examples.description: Pixel Canyon: you fly down a canyon built of a broken signal, walls and floor of blocks lit in a data pattern, towards a white-hot horizon. A strong event collapses it (RGB parts, rows drift, the walls shatter into blocks, a wave of colour passes through you) and it rebuilds turned a quarter turn, recoloured and re-patterned. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/ABSTRACT-PLAN.md.
examples.name: Sonic Abstract - Glitch Signal

examples.description: Bubble Reef: a lost 8-bit water level grown into 3D and swum through for ever -- three areas with their own palettes round a deep basin -- that plays along with the music: the bass bends the kelp, a melody rings a row of bell flowers, a chord blooms the coral, drums burst bubbles and flash the treasure, and a big friendly fish circling over the lane swims the melody. Live: opening it turns live input on (View > Live). See docs/prototypes/sonic-garden/ABSTRACT-PLAN.md.
examples.name: Sonic Abstract - 8-Bit Ocean

examples.description: THE RIFT: a drained abyssal trench alive with bioluminescent life on Trench. The music travels through it as waves of light, the canopy answers late, and the drop ignites the whole canyon. Needs assets/audio/trench.wav. See docs/prototypes/bioluminescent/.
examples.name: THE RIFT (Bioluminescent Environment)

examples.description: Play any music with a clear build and drop into the live input (BlackHole or a mixer feed). MIDI: CC1 sensitivity, CC2 wave speed, CC3 how easily the ecosystem fires, CC4 how much light floods the canyon; pads 36-42 force a stage (Dark ... Drop ... Aftermath).
examples.name: THE RIFT LIVE
